platforms.name: macOS
platforms.description: AppKit's controls of macOS 26 and 27, measured from AppKit's own rendering on macOS 27.2 in a key window.

platforms.name: Windows
platforms.description: WinUI 3's Fluent 2 controls of Windows 11, from the theme resources of microsoft-ui-xaml, the core controls compared with WinUI 3's own rendering.

platforms.name: Linux
platforms.description: GNOME's libadwaita controls, from the libadwaita 1.10 stylesheet (GTK 4.24, adwaita-icon-theme 51), compared pixel by pixel with libadwaita 1.10.0's own rendering.

components.name: Accordion
components.description: Sections that open and close one above the other, Up and Down moving between their headers: a section of a grouped form on macOS, as NSBox and System Settings draw it, Expander cards 4 DIPs apart on Windows 11, or a boxed list on GNOME. The headers and their arrows are MyGo's.

components.name: AccordionItem
components.description: A section of an Accordion: a row under a separator inset 10 points on macOS, an Expander's card on Windows 11, a row of a boxed list on GNOME; its header is MyGo's.

components.name: ActionRow
components.description: A settings row: a title, an optional subtitle below it and controls at its end, drawn as a row of a grouped form in System Settings on macOS, CommunityToolkit's SettingsCard on Windows 11, or AdwActionRow on GNOME. Rows one after another in a Card, a Fieldset or an AccordionItem join as the platform joins them: a section with inset separators, SettingsCards 4 DIPs apart or a SettingsExpander's items, a boxed list.

components.name: AlertDialog
components.description: An alert with a title, a message and buttons, the last the default: macOS's NSAlert, Windows 11's ContentDialog with the default button first, or GNOME's AdwAlertDialog. The index returned is the same on every platform.

components.name: Autocomplete
components.description: A text input suggesting the options that contain what was typed, in the platform's text field box: macOS's bezeled field, Windows 11's TextBox or GNOME's entry; the suggestions show in the platform's menu: NSMenu's panel and rows, an AutoSuggestBox's list of ListViewItems, or a dropdown's popover.

components.name: Avatar
components.description: A picture of a person or a thing: the image in a circle, or initials as the platform draws a contact without one: macOS's gray monogram, Windows 11's PersonPicture, or GNOME's AdwAvatar on a gradient picked from the name.

components.name: BackButton
components.description: A button going back in a router's history, disabled at its start, its right click listing the pages before: a macOS toolbar item, a 36-point platter with a hairline around SF Symbols' chevron, shared with ForwardButton in a Toolbar, Windows 11's NavigationView back button with its arrow, or GNOME's flat image button with go-previous-symbolic, as in a header bar.

components.name: Badge
components.description: A small label for a count: Windows 11's InfoBadge in the accent color, GNOME's indicator badge; macOS has no badge control of its own and keeps MyGo's.

components.name: Breadcrumbs
components.description: A path whose items but the last are links: macOS's NSPathControl in secondaryLabelColor with chevrons, Windows 11's BreadcrumbBar, or the path bar of GNOME's Files, bold buttons separated by slashes in a trough.

components.name: Button
components.description: A push button: macOS's push button, Windows 11's button with its elevation border, or GNOME's text button; in a Toolbar, the platform's toolbar item: a 36-point capsule on macOS, an AppBarButton on Windows 11, a raised text button on GNOME.

components.name: Calendar
components.description: A month's calendar choosing a day: package ui's, laid out as SwiftUI's graphical date picker, in the platform's theme. Its days and buttons are built inside it, out of reach of a style applied to what it returns, and a calendar rebuilt outside MyGo could neither name its month buttons in MyGo's translations nor take Browse, which acts only on MyGo's own calendar, so it is not drawn as NSDatePicker's calendar, WinUI's CalendarView or GtkCalendar: CalendarView draws them.

components.name: CalendarView
components.description: A month's calendar choosing a day, drawn as the platform draws its own: NSDatePicker's graphical calendar on macOS (the abbreviated month and year with ◀ ● ▶, short day names over a line, the chosen day a rounded rectangle, today's number in the accent), WinUI's CalendarView on Windows 11 (40-DIP round day items, today a filled accent circle, the chosen day an accent ring, up and down buttons), or GtkCalendar on GNOME (arrows around the month and the year, the chosen day filled with the accent, today underlined). Month and day names, the first day of the week and the numbers follow the window's language and the user's region. The arrows, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End move as the platform's calendar does, choosing as they move on macOS; Enter, Space or a click choose.

components.name: Card
components.description: A card around content that belongs together: SwiftUI's GroupBox on macOS, the card of WinUI's Expander and SettingsCard on Windows 11, or a .card on GNOME. Rows built in it join into the platform's list.

components.name: Checkbox
components.description: A check box with a label, sized and filled as the platform draws its own.

components.name: CheckboxGroup
components.description: A check box over the check boxes it groups, checked when they all are and mixed when some are: the platform's check box, with macOS's mixed dash, Windows 11's indeterminate glyph or GNOME's dash.svg, over the boxes built with breeze.Checkbox, indented below its label (24 DIPs on Windows 11, as WinUI Gallery's three-state sample). Rebuilt on ui.CheckboxBase; it counts only the boxes built with breeze.Checkbox.

components.name: Collapsible
components.description: A disclosure showing its content while open: macOS's disclosure chevron beside its label, Windows 11's Expander with its header card and chevron button, or GNOME's GtkExpander arrow.

components.name: ColorPicker
components.description: A picker of a color with a saturation and brightness square, hue and opacity sliders, the hex and swatches: package ui's, laid out as AppKit's color panel, in the platform's theme. Its parts are built inside it, and a picker rebuilt outside MyGo could not name them, their values and the swatches' colors in MyGo's translations. WinUI's ColorPicker and GTK's color chooser lay theirs out differently.

components.name: ColorWell
components.description: A swatch of a color opening a picker below it: macOS's NSColorWell, a capsule in a capsule; on Windows 11, which has no color well, a DropDownButton showing the color; GNOME's GtkColorDialogButton. The picker it opens is MyGo's.

components.name: ComboRow
components.description: A settings row choosing one of a list, the choice at its end: a grouped form's Picker on macOS (the choice before a circle with up and down chevrons), a SettingsCard holding a ComboBox on Windows 11, or AdwComboRow on GNOME, where the whole row opens the list. It joins a Card, a Fieldset or an AccordionItem as ActionRow does.

components.name: Combobox
components.description: A field whose text filters a list of options, in the platform's text field box; the list is MyGo's.

components.name: ContentRow
components.description: A settings row holding content below its label, such as a text area or a list: a VStack row of a grouped form on macOS, a SettingsCard with ContentAlignment Vertical on Windows 11 (the content 8 below the header, stretched), or a boxed-list row built of AdwActionRow's header on GNOME. It joins a Card, a Fieldset, an AccordionItem or a PreferencesGroup as ActionRow does.

components.name: DateInput
components.description: A field showing a date that opens a calendar: macOS's NSDatePicker of style textField, without an icon, Windows 11's CalendarDatePicker, or a GNOME entry with its icon at 70%, as GTK has no date field. The calendar is MyGo's.

components.name: DatePicker
components.description: A button showing a date in the user's short format that opens CalendarView in a popover below it: the date field of SwiftUI's compact DatePicker on macOS, WinUI's CalendarDatePicker with its calendar glyph and flyout on Windows 11, or a GtkMenuButton with a pan-down arrow opening a GtkCalendar on GNOME. Choosing a day closes it; a zero date shows WinUI's placeholder, select a date.

components.name: DecimalInput
components.description: A field editing an exact decimal, as an amount of money, with buttons stepping it: package ui's, in the platform's theme. Its field and buttons are built inside it, out of reach of a style applied to what it returns, and a field rebuilt outside MyGo could not show its errors (Enter a number, Use at most 2 decimal places) in MyGo's translations, while NumberInput, which shows none, is rebuilt.

components.name: Divider
components.description: A line between parts of a view in the platform's separator color: separatorColor, DividerStrokeColorDefault or $border_color.

components.name: EditableText
components.description: A text edited in place, as a file's name in Finder: package ui's, with MyGo's accent border around the input covered while it is edited and the platform's frame drawn there: AppKit's focus ring, a focused WinUI TextBox's edge and accent line, nothing around GTK's editable label. The input's fill and caret are MyGo's.

components.name: EntryRow
components.description: A settings row editing a text, named by its title: a grouped form's TextField with a label on macOS (the text at the trailing edge, no bezel), a SettingsCard holding a TextBox on Windows 11, or AdwEntryRow on GNOME, its title shrinking above the text as the row is focused or filled. It joins a Card, a Fieldset or an AccordionItem as ActionRow does.

components.name: ExpanderRow
components.description: A settings row that opens to show the rows built in it: a grouped form's DisclosureGroup on macOS, CommunityToolkit's SettingsExpander on Windows 11, or AdwExpanderRow on GNOME, each with the platform's own header and arrow. Alone it is a group of its own; in a Card, a Fieldset or an AccordionItem it joins as a row does.

components.name: Field
components.description: A labeled control: in a Form the labels line up before the controls as in a macOS form; elsewhere the label is above, 8 DIPs on Windows 11 at regular weight as a TextBox's header.

components.name: Fieldset
components.description: A group of fields under a legend: a grouped form section on macOS (NSBox's fill), the fields under a Body Strong header on Windows 11, which has no group box, or a card under an AdwPreferencesGroup's bold title on GNOME.

components.name: FindBar
components.description: A bar for finding text, in the platform's place for it: NSTextFinder's find bar on macOS, GtkSearchBar's bar on GNOME, a strip with a divider on Windows 11, which has none. The field, the buttons and the keys are MyGo's, in the platform's theme: a bar rebuilt outside MyGo could not say its names and its count (Find, No matches, 2 of 5, Previous, Next, Done) in MyGo's translations.

components.name: Form
components.description: A column of fields: the labels in a column before the controls on macOS and GNOME, as ui.Form lays them out, and above the controls on Windows 11, 12 DIPs between fields, as its controls take their headers.

components.name: ForwardButton
components.description: A button going forward in a router's history, drawn as BackButton is on each platform, its glyph pointing the other way.

components.name: GridView
components.description: A scrolling grid of items built as they show, each drawn as the platform draws its own: Windows 11's GridViewItem with its 2-DIP accent border, GNOME's GtkGridView child with its accent-tinted fill, and on macOS, where NSCollectionView draws no selection, an inset table's rounded selection (inferred). The choice, the keys and accessibility are MyGo's, as are the items' gap and size.

components.name: HeaderBar
components.description: The title bar a view draws in a window whose title bar is hidden (mygo.WindowOptions.TitleBarStyle): a title, an optional subtitle and controls before and after it, keeping clear of the window controls in c.TitleBar()'s room and moving the window when dragged outside its controls. It is drawn as a macOS window's unified toolbar showing its title (52 points high, the title after the start controls), Windows 11's TitleBar control (48 DIPs high with controls, the title in the caption style after them), or GNOME's AdwHeaderBar (47 pixels high, the title centered); breeze's buttons inside take the title bar's look.

components.name: IconButton
components.description: A button showing only an icon, the caller's SVG tinted with the button's text color, its label naming it and showing as its tooltip: macOS's bordered push button with an image, Windows 11's Button with a 16-DIP icon, or GNOME's 34-pixel image button; in a Toolbar, the platform's image item (an NSToolbar image item, an icon-only AppBarButton, a flat image button).

components.name: InfoBar
components.description: An inline message bar with a severity, a title and a message, optionally closable: Windows 11's InfoBar colored by its severity, GNOME's AdwBanner (banners have no severity), or on macOS, which has no message bar, a grouped form section with a colored SF Symbol (inferred). The severity is a toast's Type: "success", "warning", "error" or informational.

components.name: Link
components.description: Text that opens a URL in the platform's link color: AppKit's linkColor, Windows 11's AccentTextFillColorPrimary with its pointer-over and pressed shades, libadwaita's accent_color; underlined on Windows and GNOME.

components.name: List
components.description: A scrolling list of rows built as they show: macOS's inset NSTableView with its rounded selection, Windows 11's ListView with the accent pill on the chosen item, or GNOME's GtkListView with the accent-tinted row. The choice, the keys and accessibility are MyGo's.

components.name: MenuButton
components.description: A button drawn as the platform's pull-down button with its chevron, or as a toolbar item in a Toolbar, opening the system's own native menu.

components.name: Meter
components.description: A bar showing a level, with warning and critical levels: macOS's NSLevelIndicator in green, yellow or red, Windows 11's ProgressBar in its normal, paused or error color, or GNOME's GtkLevelBar.
components.example: breeze.Meter(c, app.used, 0, app.size, &ui.MeterLevels{Warning: 0.8 * app.size, Critical: 0.95 * app.size}).Label("Disk")

components.name: Modal
components.description: A dialog over the window: a sheet with a window's shadow on macOS, which leaves the window undimmed, a ContentDialog on Windows 11, or a floating AdwDialog over a dimmed window on GNOME.

components.name: NumberInput
components.description: A field editing a number with buttons stepping it: an NSTextField with an NSStepper beside it on macOS, a NumberBox with its inline spin buttons on Windows 11, or a GtkSpinButton with − and + after the text on GNOME. Rebuilt from ui.TextInputBase and ui.ButtonBase as ui.NumberInput is, with its keys, Tab order and Decrease and Increase buttons.

components.name: Outline
components.description: A list of items in a tree, built as they show: macOS's inset NSOutlineView with its rounded selection and turning chevron, Windows 11's TreeView with its backplate and accent pill, or GNOME's GtkListView rows with a GtkTreeExpander's pan icons. The chevron is drawn in MyGo's arrow box; the choice, the keys and accessibility are MyGo's, as are the rows' padding and gaps.

components.name: OutlineTable
components.description: An outline whose rows are a table's, its chevrons in the first column: its rows drawn as Table draws them and its chevrons as Outline does. The header is MyGo's, in the platform's theme.

components.name: PasswordField
components.description: A single-line field hiding its text in the platform's text field: macOS's NSSecureTextField, Windows 11's PasswordBox with its RevealButton (shown while text typed since the focus came, revealing while pressed or Alt+F8 is held), or GNOME's GtkPasswordEntry with Show Text in its context menu.

components.name: Popover
components.description: A panel beside an element: a menu-like panel on macOS, Windows 11's FlyoutPresenter, or a libadwaita popover.

components.name: PopoverMenuButton
components.description: A button drawn as the platform's pull-down button with its chevron, or as a toolbar item in a Toolbar, opening a menu MyGo draws in the window in the platform's menu colors and corners.

components.name: PreferencesGroup
components.description: A group of settings rows under a header with controls at the end of its line and a description: a grouped form's Section with a header and a footer on macOS, a settings section with its header and cards on Windows 11, or AdwPreferencesGroup with its header suffix and description on GNOME. Its rows join as a Fieldset's do.

components.name: PrefixRow
components.description: An ActionRow with content before its title, such as an icon, an avatar or a tile: a grouped form's row with an image on macOS (10 in, the title 10 after it), a SettingsCard's HeaderIcon on Windows 11, or AdwActionRow's prefixes on GNOME. It joins a group as ActionRow does, its separators unbroken.

components.name: PrimaryButton
components.description: The main action in the accent color: macOS's default button, Windows 11's accent button or GNOME's suggested action; in a Toolbar, the platform's toolbar item.

components.name: Progress
components.description: A progress bar, or a moving one for a negative value: macOS's bar, Windows 11's thin ProgressBar, or GNOME's progress bar.

components.name: ProgressRing
components.description: A circular progress indicator filled to a value from 0 to 1: macOS's determinate spinning NSProgressIndicator, Windows 11's ProgressRing with IsIndeterminate false, or on GNOME, which has none, a ring after AdwSpinner in the accent (inferred). A negative value shows the Spinner.

components.name: Radio
components.description: A radio button with a label: macOS's 16-point radio button, Windows 11's RadioButton with its growing dot, or GNOME's grouped check button.

components.name: RadioGroup
components.description: The group radio buttons choose within, which the arrows move through, its radio buttons set as far apart as the platform sets them: 6 points down a column and 8 across a row on macOS, as SwiftUI's radio-group picker; RadioButtons' row spacing 8 and column spacing 7 on Windows 11; the padded check buttons next to each other on GNOME, which has no radio group.

components.name: RadioRow
components.description: A settings row choosing a value, one of the radio rows sharing it, a click anywhere on the row choosing it and Up and Down moving among those of its group: a radio-group Picker's row on macOS, the radio button at its trailing edge; a clickable SettingsCard with a RadioButton as its HeaderIcon on Windows 11; or AdwActionRow with a grouped check button as its prefix on GNOME. Assistive technology sees one radio button named by its title.

components.name: RangeSlider
components.description: A slider of two knobs setting a range: package ui's, in the platform's accent and colors. Its knobs take the focus as elements inside it, whose focus rings only MyGo's drawing can show, and knobs rebuilt outside MyGo could not be named after the slider's Label (Price minimum), so it is not drawn as the platforms' sliders; macOS and GNOME have no range slider, Windows its Community Toolkit's RangeSelector.

components.name: Rating
components.description: A row of stars setting a rating: macOS's NSLevelIndicator of rating style, Windows 11's RatingControl with its accent stars, or GNOME Software's stars, as GNOME has no rating control. The clicks and keys are MyGo's.

components.name: Scroll
components.description: A container scrolling its children vertically: package ui's, its scroll bar painted by MyGo in the platform's scroll bar color and width (the overlay knob's black or white at 50% on macOS, WinUI's ScrollBarThumbFill, GNOME's 3-pixel slider at 20%). MyGo paints the bar itself from the theme alone, so its thickness, track, arrows and growth under the pointer are MyGo's on every platform.

components.name: ScrollBoth
components.description: A container scrolling its children both ways, as a canvas or a wide table does: package ui's, its two scroll bars painted by MyGo in the platform's scroll bar color and width, as Scroll's.

components.name: ScrollHorizontal
components.description: A row scrolling its children horizontally: package ui's, its scroll bar painted by MyGo in the platform's scroll bar color and width, as Scroll's.

components.name: SearchField
components.description: A search field with a magnifying glass and a clear button: macOS's capsule search field, Windows 11's AutoSuggestBox, or GNOME's search entry.

components.name: Segmented
components.description: A segmented control choosing one of a few views: macOS's NSSegmentedControl, the chosen segment in the accent color as a key window draws it, Windows 11's SelectorBar, or GNOME's AdwToggleGroup.

components.name: Select
components.description: A drop-down choosing one of a list: macOS's pop-up button and menu, Windows 11's ComboBox with its accent pill, or GNOME's drop-down and popover.

components.name: Sidebar
components.description: A sidebar of sections and items, which the arrows and typing choose among: macOS's source list, its selection in the accent color while it has the focus and gray otherwise, Windows 11's NavigationView pane, or GNOME's AdwSidebar.

components.name: SidebarItem
components.description: An item of a Sidebar with an optional icon: a 32-point source list row on macOS, its label semibold when chosen, a NavigationViewItem with its accent pill on Windows 11, a 42-pixel AdwSidebar row on GNOME.

components.name: SidebarSection
components.description: A section of a Sidebar that its title shows and hides, headed as the platform heads one: AppKit's group row, Windows 11's NavigationViewItemHeader, or AdwSidebar's bold heading on GNOME.

components.name: Slider
components.description: A slider setting a value in a range: macOS's capsule knob, Windows 11's thumb with its accent dot, or GNOME's scale.

components.name: SpinRow
components.description: A settings row setting a number between limits with stepping buttons, its text the one focus stop: a grouped form's Stepper with its value in a text field on macOS, a SettingsCard holding a NumberBox on Windows 11, or AdwSpinRow on GNOME, with circular − and + buttons. It joins a Card, a Fieldset or an AccordionItem as ActionRow does.

components.name: Spinner
components.description: An indicator of work of unknown length: macOS's spokes, Windows 11's ProgressRing, or GNOME's AdwSpinner.

components.name: Split
components.description: Two panes side by side with a divider that a drag or the arrows move: MyGo's 1-DIP line in the theme's border color, 1 wide as NSSplitView's thin divider and GtkPaned's separator are, which stays that color under the pointer and while dragged, as on every platform, where MyGo's turns to the accent. It grabs 6 DIPs.

components.name: SplitButton
components.description: A button of two parts, the main action, which Clicked reports, and an arrow opening the system's own menu: macOS's NSComboButton of style split, Windows 11's SplitButton, or GNOME's AdwSplitButton; in a Toolbar, the platform's toolbar split button.

components.name: SplitPercent
components.description: Split with the first pane's share of the room in percent, its divider in the border color under the pointer too.

components.name: SplitVertical
components.description: Split with the first pane above the second, its divider in the border color under the pointer too.

components.name: SplitVerticalPercent
components.description: SplitPercent with the first pane above the second, its divider in the border color under the pointer too.

components.name: StatusPage
components.description: An empty-state page with an icon, a title, a description and actions below them: GNOME's AdwStatusPage, SwiftUI's ContentUnavailableView on macOS, or on Windows 11, which has no such control, a page after WinUI's type ramp (inferred).

components.name: StepSlider
components.description: A slider that snaps to steps with a tick mark at each: macOS's NSSlider with dots below its track, Windows 11's Slider with ticks below (TickPlacement BottomRight), or GNOME's GtkScale with marks and a pointed slider.

components.name: Stepper
components.description: Arrows stepping a number: the box is the platform's (NSStepper on macOS, a button's face elsewhere); the arrows, holding to repeat and the keys are MyGo's.

components.name: Switch
components.description: A switch with the platform's track, knob and motion: a capsule knob on macOS, a growing knob on Windows, a round slider on GNOME.

components.name: SwitchRow
components.description: A settings row with a switch at its end that a click anywhere on the row toggles, one switch for assistive technology named by its title: a grouped form's Toggle with its mini switch on macOS, a SettingsCard with a ToggleSwitch and its On or Off text on Windows 11, or AdwSwitchRow on GNOME.

components.name: TabView
components.description: Document tabs that close, with a button adding one; build the chosen tab's content after it: the tab bar of a window's tabs on macOS (a capsule track, the chosen tab raised, the close button under the pointer at the leading edge, the + button after it), WinUI's TabView on Windows 11 (the chosen tab joined to the strip's line by curved corners, close buttons on every tab, the add button after the tabs), or AdwTabBar on GNOME (tabs sharing the bar, the close button on the chosen tab and under the pointer, the new tab button at its end). Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab switch tabs, Ctrl+F4 closes one on Windows, and GNOME's Ctrl+Page Up, Ctrl+Page Down and Alt+digits choose one.

components.name: Table
components.description: A table of rows and columns whose rows are drawn as the platform draws them: macOS's inset NSTableView with its rounded selection, Windows 11's ListView items with their backplate and accent pill, or GNOME's GtkColumnView with the accent-tinted row. The choice, the sort, the columns and accessibility are MyGo's, as are the header, the cells' padding and the rows' least height.

components.name: Tabs
components.description: Tabs choosing a page: macOS's tab view with the chosen tab on a raised platter, Windows 11's SelectorBar, or GNOME's notebook tabs.

components.name: Text
components.description: A text in a step of the platform's type ramp: TextLargeTitle, TextTitle, TextSubtitle, TextHeading, TextBody or TextCaption, drawn in macOS's text styles (largeTitle 26 points, title1 22, title2 17, headline 13 bold, body 13, caption1 10), Windows 11's TextBlock styles (TitleLarge 40, Title 28, Subtitle 20 and BodyStrong 14 in semibold, Body 14, Caption 12) or libadwaita's classes (.title-1, .title-2, .title-4, .heading, a plain label, .caption), in the theme's font. TextSecondary added with | dims a step as secondaryLabelColor, TextFillColorSecondary or .dimmed do. The style comes after the text and can be left out: without one it is TextBody, which draws what ui.Text draws, so breeze.Text(c, s) replaces ui.Text(c, s); wrapping, selection and right-to-left text are ui.Text's.
components.example:
breeze.Text(c, "Settings", breeze.TextTitle)
breeze.Text(c, "Applies to every window.", breeze.TextCaption|breeze.TextSecondary)

components.name: TextArea
components.description: A multi-line text input in the platform's text view: a bezel-bordered view on macOS, a TextBox on Windows 11, a framed view on GNOME.

components.name: TextAreaBuffer
components.description: A multi-line text input editing a ui.TextBuffer, whose edits never copy the whole document, in the same text view as TextArea: a bezel-bordered view on macOS, a TextBox on Windows 11, a framed view on GNOME. Editing, undo, the selection, input methods and scrolling are MyGo's.

components.name: TextInput
components.description: A single-line text input in the platform's field: macOS's bezeled field with its focus ring, Windows 11's TextBox with the accent line, or GNOME's filled entry.

components.name: TextInputBuffer
components.description: A single-line text input editing a ui.TextBuffer, in the same field as TextInput: macOS's bezeled field with its focus ring, Windows 11's TextBox with the accent line, or GNOME's filled entry. Editing, undo, the selection and input methods are MyGo's.

components.name: TimeInput
components.description: A field of a time of day whose hours, minutes and half of the day each take the focus: in macOS's NSDatePicker bezel, Windows 11's TimePicker button, 242 wide with the segments spread across it, or a GNOME entry. The segments, their keys and the colon between the hours and the minutes are MyGo's.

components.name: Toasts
components.description: The window's toasts in the platform's look: GNOME's AdwToast pill, Windows 11's InfoBar colored by the toast's type, or on macOS, which has no toast, a panel like a notification banner.

components.name: Toggle
components.description: A button that stays pressed: macOS's push-on-push-off button, in the accent color while on as a key window draws it, Windows 11's ToggleButton in the accent color, or GNOME's checked toggle button; in a Toolbar, the platform's toolbar item.

components.name: ToggleGroup
components.description: Toggles joined as the platform joins them: an NSSegmentedControl selecting any segments on macOS, a box.linked on GNOME, ToggleButtons side by side on Windows 11, which has no joined toggles.

components.name: TokenField
components.description: A field of tokens, as of tags, in the platform's text field box: macOS's bezeled field, Windows 11's TextBox or GNOME's entry. The chips and the suggestions are MyGo's in the platform's theme, not NSTokenField's or TokenizingTextBox's tokens; GNOME has no token field.

components.name: Toolbar
components.description: A row of controls along the top of a window, which the arrows move among and which puts those that do not fit in a menu, its buttons, toggles and menu buttons drawn as the platform's toolbar items: 52 points high with 36-point capsules 8 apart as a macOS window's toolbar, adjacent image items sharing a platter, Windows 11's CommandBar with AppBarButtons, or GNOME's .toolbar with flat image buttons.

components.name: Tooltip
components.description: A tip shown while the pointer rests on an element: a small panel below it on macOS, Windows 11's ToolTip above it, or GTK's dark tooltip below it on GNOME.

components.name: Tree
components.description: A tree of items that open and close, its rows drawn as the platform draws a tree's: an inset NSOutlineView's rounded selection, Windows 11's TreeView backplate, or GNOME's GtkListView rows. MyGo's TreeItem takes the platform's row colors from a theme the tree builds its items in; the keys and accessibility are MyGo's.

components.name: TreeItem
components.description: An item of a Tree, at the platform's row height, insets, corners and indentation. MyGo's disclosure arrow stays, and WinUI's accent pill on the chosen item is not drawn.

components.name: ViewSwitcher
components.description: The control that switches an app's top-level views, each a breeze.ViewItem of an icon and a label; build the chosen view after it, and put it in a HeaderBar's end controls or a Toolbar to switch the window's views from there. It is drawn as macOS's NSToolbarItemGroup of selectionMode selectOne in a toolbar (one platter of 37-point image segments, the chosen one a gray pill, the labels naming them) and its NSSegmentedControl elsewhere (icons before the labels), Windows 11's SelectorBar (icon and text, the accent pill under the chosen item), or GNOME's AdwViewSwitcher in its wide policy (flat buttons at least 120 wide, the icon beside the bold label, the chosen one filled). Tab stops once at the chosen item and the arrows choose among them; assistive technology sees a radio group on macOS and a tab list elsewhere, each item named by its label.
components.example:
breeze.ViewSwitcher(c, &app.view,
	breeze.ViewItem{Icon: libraryIcon, Label: "Library"},
	breeze.ViewItem{Icon: browseIcon, Label: "Browse"},
	breeze.ViewItem{Icon: radioIcon, Label: "Radio"},
)
